speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have experienced occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings following your tympanoplasty; to help me evaluate your condition, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and how frequently they occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia (specifically involving the V3 branch affecting the auriculotemporal nerve).

The shooting pain triggered by chewing and the specific discomfort with earrings in a post-tympanoplasty patient strongly suggest neuralgia or nerve entrapment rather than simple infection. Would you like me to order a CT scan of the temporal bone to evaluate the surgical site and rule out ossicular issues or nerve compression?
